text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Tursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Romania is surrounded by areas where tension has climaxed, newspaper says about street protests in Serbia, Bulgaria and Albania.
- Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea will appear on television, with IMF and World Bank representatives, to explain the need for austerity steps and say where the economy is going.
- The government has suspended taxes on farming incomes until the year 2000, in keeping with its electoral promises.
- PM Ciorbea will meet the IMF mission on Thursday, ahead of press conference at the government's headquarters. Later in the day he will also make a televised appearance.
- The Romanian commercial bank CEC raises deposit rates starting February.
- Romania's CNVM securities regulator plans to privatise the Bucharest stock exchange and to turn the Rasdaq over-the-counter trading system into a shareholding company.
- The leu currency lost 68 percent against the dollar in the past three months -- its sharpest ever depreciation.
- After Belgrade, Sofia and Tirana, will it be Bucharest's turn? asks newspaper director Ion Cristoiu in his editorial.
- "Romania can be a strong stabilising force in central Europe," the newspaper quotes visiting British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind as saying in interview.
- "The price of the free leu," says newspaper editorial about the economic and political impact of the local currency's sharp devaluation in recent months.
